facts: Portofino is a picturesque fishing village located on the Italian Riviera in the Liguria region.
The village is famous for its vibrant pastel colored houses surrounding a sheltered crescent shaped harbor.
Castello Brown, a sixteenth century fortress overlooking the harbor, offers stunning panoramic views of the Ligurian Coast.
Portofino Regional Natural Park features over sixty kilometers of scenic hiking trails through lush Mediterranean vegetation.
The Marine Protected Area of Portofino safeguards rich underwater biodiversity making it popular for scuba diving.
Ancient Romans founded the village and named it Portus Delphini because of the many dolphins in the gulf.
Pesto alla Genovese, made with fresh local basil, pine nuts, garlic, and olive oil, originated in this region.
The Church of Saint George houses relics of Saint George brought back by local sailors from the Crusades.
Traditional Ligurian Focaccia is a popular local savory bread enjoyed fresh from village bakeries every morning.
Portofino became a luxury resort destination in the nineteen fifties, attracting international celebrities, artists, and royalty.
The iconic Christ of the Abyss statue rests underwater nearby to protect sailors and divers in the bay.
Focaccia col Formaggio, a crispy flatbread filled with creamy local cheese, is a famous regional delicacy nearby.
Running along the coastal roads near Portofino rewards you with dramatic sea cliffs and salty Mediterranean breezes.
Local vineyards cultivate Bianchetta Genovese grapes to produce refreshing white wines that pair perfectly with seafood.
The San Fruttuoso Abbey, accessible only by boat or on foot, sits tucked in a secluded cove nearby.
Classical composer Richard Wagner drew creative inspiration from the serene beauty of the Portofino peninsula.
The Piazzetta is the bustling central heart of Portofino where travelers gather for espresso and people watching.
High cliffs around the promontory create challenging elevation changes that are great for building runner leg strength.
The traditional red, yellow, and terracotta paint on harbor buildings historically helped fishermen identify their homes.
Portofino Mediterranean climate allows for pleasant outdoor running conditions throughout most of the year.
